record.narrative: No prior claims exist. This first round registers a balanced discovery screen for common binary predictors and a few effect-modification hypotheses. Outcomes are selected for informative variance and distinct score distributions: outcome_014 (least negative mean), outcome_006 (broad spread), outcome_001 (more negative mean and wide spread), and outcome_013 (heavy-tailed negative dependency). Exposure feature_002, feature_034, feature_060, feature_045, and feature_021 are common binary labels with enough rows for Welch discovery. Direction convention: more negative dependency score means stronger dependency; a negative hypothesis direction means exposed-minus-comparator is expected to be more negative, and a positive direction means exposed is expected to have a less negative score. Because predictor labels are opaque, I deliberately register both biologically plausible directions: marker presence for feature_002/feature_060/feature_021 is hypothesized to increase dependency, while marker presence for feature_034/feature_045 is hypothesized to decrease dependency. Plausible alternatives include the opposite sign, a null main effect, or a subgroup-only effect. The three interaction proposals test whether the dependency contrast for feature_002 differs by feature_034 or feature_060, and whether the feature_034 contrast differs in high versus lower feature_044. These are dataset-specific associations only; causality and generalizability are not assumed.

No claim has direct evidence yet and no assessment is due. I request analysis of all twelve registered discovery comparisons because this is the first evidence batch and the registered set is already limited to 12 scientifically motivated tests: main effects for common binary predictors on the selected high-information dependency outcomes, plus three prespecified effect-modification interactions. Running all registered comparisons now gives the discovery evidence needed to prioritize follow-up; main effects and interactions will be appraised jointly after analysis.

No discovery interval excludes zero, so no claim is accepted yet. Interpreting the estimates as already signed to the hypothesis direction, H4 is the most informative result: feature_002=1 versus 0 is associated with a signed outcome_006 difference of +0.0209. Because the hypothesis direction was -1, the underlying raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is more negative, meaning stronger dependency. The point estimate is roughly around or above a 10% relative difference on the outcome_006 scale, but its 95% interval crosses zero and the screen involved multiple tests, so I keep H4 unresolved and request independent validation rather than accept it. H12 has a positive interaction trend (signed estimate +0.0333), but it is below the approximate 10% relative threshold for outcome_001 and the interval is wide, so it remains unresolved/deferred. H3 has the wrong-magnitude problem: it is signed positive but only +0.0063, well below the clinically meaningful scale for outcome_014. Most other estimates are near zero or opposite the claimed direction. There is no apparent leakage: the unique-ID-like feature_003 was not used, all cells meet the 20-observation rule, and missingness in unused features did not affect these binary comparisons. The main limitations are multiplicity and unadjusted associations; correlated predictors could produce apparent feature effects. H4 validation is the best single use of validation now. If H4 replicates, I will test feature_002 across other dependency outcomes and consider adjusted or stratified analyses; if it does not replicate, I will close it and broaden predictor exploration. Potential opposite or subgroup signals, such as H10 and H12, are not being escalated immediately because they are post hoc or underpowered, but H12 is deferred rather than closed in case stratified follow-up is informative after H4 is resolved.

New validation R13 does not support H4. H4 was the hypothesis that feature_002=1 versus 0 is associated with a more negative outcome_006 dependency score than feature_002=0. The signed validation estimate is -0.0123 on the H4 direction scale; because the hypothesis direction was -1, this corresponds to the opposite of the anticipated stronger-dependency signal. The multiplicity-adjusted validation interval is wide and crosses zero, and the validation point is roughly below a 10% relative threshold on the outcome_006 scale. This contrasts with the discovery point estimate +0.0209, which was direction-consistent and around the 10% threshold but not statistically decisive. The independent validation therefore turns the sole Round-1 discovery candidate into an inconsistent or false-positive signal, so I reject H4 as evidence for a clinically meaningful feature_002-outcome_006 association in this dataset. This rejection does not prove a null small effect; it means the available evidence does not support accepting the claimed association or extrapolating it causally. More broadly, Round 1 yielded no accepted claims: H1-H3, H5-H11 were rejected as null, small, or direction-inconsistent, and H12 remains unresolved/deferred because it showed a positive interaction trend but below the approximate 10% relative threshold and with a wide interval. Next, I registered a targeted refinement of H12: the feature_034 main effect restricted to high feature_044, which can test whether the interaction trend reflects a localized stronger-dependency signal. I also registered a focused screen of untested common binary predictors on outcome_012, selected because its lower standard deviation gives reasonable power for the 10% relative threshold and because outcome_012 was not tested in Round 1. These proposals initially test marker presence versus absence with a stronger-dependency orientation; anticipated directions are uncertain because predictor semantics are opaque, and opposite-direction claims can be registered if informative signals emerge.

No assessment is due. The main scientific update is that Round 1 produced no supported claims: H4 failed independent validation after an initial discovery trend, so binary common-feature screening cannot be treated as a validated signal pipeline. H12 is the only effect-modification result worth following. Its signed estimate was positive under direction -1, meaning the raw feature_034 contrast was more negative in the high feature_044 subgroup than in its complement. A natural refinement is to test the complementary low feature_044 subgroup. If the interaction reflects localized stronger dependency in high feature_044, the low-subgroup main effect may be smaller, positive, or near zero; I therefore register the low feature_044 main effect of feature_034 with direction +1, anticipating a positive raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast, i.e. less negative dependency in feature_034=1 than feature_034=0 in the low subgroup. This is not claimed to be clinically important yet; it is a diagnostic refinement of H12. For new discovery, I broaden Round 2 screening using outcome_012, whose standard deviation is low and whose approximate 10% relative threshold is around 0.025. I add important common binary predictors feature_002 and feature_045, selected less-tested binary predictors feature_005, feature_012, and feature_022, and nominal categorical predictors feature_054, feature_063, feature_036, feature_055, and feature_019. Categorical comparisons are level-to-reference contrasts, not ordered levels; direction -1 tests whether the exposed category is associated with a more negative dependency score. Anticipated directions are mostly uncertain because labels are opaque. These are dataset-specific associations; causality and generalizability require independent validation or replication. I will prioritize follow-up if a comparison has a signed estimate near or above 10% relative to the comparator mean with an interval that is reasonably informative, rather than accepting small interval-crossing trends from multiplicity.

No assessment is due, so I am allocating the next analysis batch to the highest-information unresolved hypotheses and to a diverse set of low-noise discovery screens. First, I request H13 and H25 to characterize H12. H12 suggested a positive signed interaction under direction -1, implying that the feature_034 contrast was more negative in high feature_044 than in the complement, but its interval crossed zero and it did not clearly exceed the approximate 10% relative threshold for outcome_001. H13 tests the high-feature_044 subgroup main effect of feature_034, while H25 tests the complementary lower-feature_044 subgroup with direction +1. Comparing these two subgroup contrasts should clarify whether H12 is a localized clinically meaningful signal, a small unstable interaction, or a null result. I also request H14, the main effect of feature_034 on outcome_012, because outcome_012 has lower variance and an approximate 10% relative threshold near 0.025; if feature_034 has no relevant main effect on this outcome but appears in outcome_001 subgroups, the interaction claim will need careful scrutiny. Second, I include H26 and H22 to test the two most common binary predictors, feature_002 and feature_060, on outcome_012. Feature_002 was the only Round-1 discovery candidate but failed independent validation on outcome_006; outcome-specific associations remain possible but require stronger evidence. Feature_060 was previously null or inconsistent for outcomes 014/006, so this is mainly a completeness screen. Third, I request H15-H18, covering less-tested binary predictors feature_042, feature_065, feature_050, and feature_037 on outcome_012. These have adequate prevalence for Welch contrasts and allow the screen to expand beyond previously explored variables. Finally, I request H31, H32, and H35 to test nominal categorical contrasts: feature_054 level_002 vs level_001, feature_063 level_002 vs level_001, and feature_055 level_001 vs level_003. These are treated as nominal label contrasts, not ordered levels. Overall, this batch balances direct follow-up on H12, completeness for common binary predictors, and diverse nominal-categorical screening. After results arrive, I will judge estimates as already signed to each claim direction, compare point estimates and intervals to approximately 10% relative thresholds on the relevant outcome scale, and treat any interval-crossing small trend as unresolved rather than accepted. Independent validation or further cross-outcome follow-up will be considered only for estimates with clinically meaningful magnitude and reasonably informative uncertainty.

No discovery interval excludes zero, so no claim is accepted now. The most important update is that the feature_034 by feature_044 interaction pathway in outcome_001 does not support a clinically meaningful localized effect. H13 estimates the high-feature_044 subgroup main effect of feature_034 with direction -1; the signed estimate is +0.0276, meaning the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is about -0.0276, i.e. stronger dependency when feature_034=1. However, this is below the approximate 10% relative scale for outcome_001, about 0.042, and its 95% interval is very wide and crosses zero. H25 tests the complementary low-feature_044 subgroup with direction +1; the signed estimate is +0.0057, very small and interval-crossing. Together, these subgroup contrasts reproduce the H12 raw interaction of about -0.0333, but both component differences are small relative to outcome_001 uncertainty and do not establish a robust effect modification. I therefore reject and close H13, H25, and the original H12 interaction claim as evidence for a scientifically meaningful feature_034/feature_044 interaction in outcome_001.  The outcome_012 binary screens are mostly null or too small. H14 feature_034, H26 feature_002, H22 feature_060, H17 feature_050, and H18 feature_037 are near zero and interval-crossing; reject. H15 feature_042 and H32 feature_063 level_002 vs level_001 have signed estimates opposite their claimed directions and below the approximate 0.025 outcome_012 threshold; reject rather than reverse because the magnitudes are not clinically compelling. H31 and H35 are direction-consistent but small and interval-crossing; reject. H16 is the only borderline candidate: feature_065=1 versus 0 on outcome_012 under direction -1 has signed estimate +0.0169, implying a more negative dependency score in the exposed group. This is below the approximate 10% threshold for outcome_012, but its interval upper bound extends above that threshold, and its lower bound is close to zero. Given the number of tested predictors, I cannot accept it, and I should not chase it as a main-effect signal on evidence alone. I request independent validation for H16 because it is the strongest remaining outcome_012 discovery candidate; validation will decide whether to escalate to cross-outcome or subgroup follow-up or close it as another multiplicity artifact. This is not a causal or generalizability claim. No leakage or coding problems are apparent: feature_003 was not used, constant feature_049 was avoided, all reported cells satisfy the minimum-size rule, and categorical levels are treated as nominal contrasts.

The independent validation of H16 is direction-consistent with the discovery trend but is not strong enough to accept as a clinically meaningful association in outcome_012. H16 tested feature_065=1 versus 0 on outcome_012 with direction -1, so a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is negative, i.e. stronger dependency when feature_065 is present. Discovery R20 gave +0.0169, 95% interval [-0.0027, +0.0365]. Validation R26 gave +0.0194 on a conservative validation-adjusted interval [-0.0094, +0.0482]. The validation point estimate is in the same direction, but it is still below the approximate 10% absolute threshold for outcome_012, about 0.025, corresponding to roughly an 8% relative shift. Moreover, the validation interval crosses zero and extends both below and above the clinical threshold. Therefore I do not accept H16: the evidence suggests a possible small stronger-dependency association, but it does not establish a scientifically meaningful 10% difference in this dataset. I keep H16 unresolved and active because cross-outcome replication could determine whether feature_065 is a broad dependency-score predictor or a single-outcome borderline artifact. I registered follow-up claims for feature_065 on outcome_015 and outcome_003, which have similar low noise and approximate 10% thresholds near 0.025. If these follow-ups are direction-consistent and clinically meaningful, I may cautiously accept outcome-specific associations. If they are null or opposite, I will reject the feature_065 signal. The next analysis batch should also continue existing registered outcome_012 screens, but small interval-crossing trends should be treated as weak unless they replicate across outcomes or have intervals clearly above threshold. No leakage or coding issue is apparent: the unique identifier and constant features were avoided, all comparison cells satisfy the minimum sample size, and estimates are being interpreted as already signed to hypothesis direction. Causality and generalizability are not claimed.

No assessments are due. The scientifically important open question is whether feature_065 is a broadly relevant predictor of CRISPR dependency or a borderline outcome-specific artifact. H16 and its validation R26 were direction-consistent for outcome_012: with direction -1, positive signed estimates mean the raw feature_065=1 minus feature_065=0 contrast is negative, i.e. stronger dependency among feature_065=1. However, both point estimates are below the approximate 10% threshold and intervals cross zero. I therefore propose six additional outcome-specific main-effect tests of feature_065=1 versus 0 on low-noise outcomes with similar approximate 10% absolute thresholds around 0.025: outcome_005, outcome_004, outcome_002, outcome_007, outcome_009, and outcome_016. For these, anticipated_direction is -1 because prior evidence suggests raw negative differences. Plausible alternatives are null, opposite, or outcome-specific patterns. If several independent outcomes show direction-consistent estimates near or above threshold with informative intervals, outcome-specific associations become more plausible; if they are mostly null or opposite, I will treat feature_065 as unsupported and reject the signal.  I also propose a new broad screen on outcome_015, which was only targeted by feature_065. The screen tests less-explored binary predictors feature_008, feature_030, feature_047, feature_023, and feature_032, plus one nominal categorical contrast feature_055 level_002 versus level_003. These comparisons are all direction -1, meaning exposed category/marker presence is hypothesized to have a more negative dependency score, but anticipated_direction is 0 because the labels are opaque. Categorical levels are nominal, not ordered. The alternatives are null, opposite, or small marker-specific effects. I will only accept new predictors if estimates are clinically meaningful and uncertainty is informative; small interval-crossing trends should remain unresolved or be rejected rather than chased. No causal or generalizability claims are implied. The unique identifier and constant predictors remain excluded, and all proposed categories are expected to have adequate cell counts.

No assessments are due, so this batch allocates all 12 analyses to the highest-information unresolved candidates. First, I request every registered feature_065 cross-outcome replication, H37-H44. H16 and its independent validation gave direction-consistent but clinically borderline stronger-dependency evidence for feature_065=1 versus 0 on outcome_012. Testing feature_065 on outcome_015, outcome_003, outcome_005, outcome_004, outcome_002, outcome_007, outcome_009, and outcome_016 should determine whether this is a coherent low-noise dependency-score association or an outcome-specific borderline artifact. Because these outcomes have similar means and standard deviations, approximate 10% thresholds are near 0.025. With direction -1, positive signed estimates mean raw stronger dependency in feature_065=1. I will not accept on a single interval-crossing trend; coherence across several outcomes or a clear interval above the clinical threshold would be needed. Second, I request four new outcome_015 screens: H45 feature_008, H46 feature_030, H47 feature_047, and H50 nominal categorical feature_055 level_002 versus level_003. These add diversity beyond feature_065 and continue broad screening on a low-noise outcome. H48 and H49 remain registered but are deferred because of the 12-test cap. All estimates will be interpreted as already signed to the hypothesis direction. Categorical levels are nominal labels, not ordered values. No causal or generalizability claim is implied by these dataset-specific contrasts.

The key new result is H37: on outcome_015, feature_065=1 versus 0 under direction -1 has signed estimate +0.0211 [0.0018, 0.0404]. This is the only newly delivered interval that excludes zero and is direction-consistent with stronger dependency in the exposed group. However, the raw absolute difference is about 0.021, roughly 8.5% of the outcome_015 mean magnitude, below the approximate 10% clinical threshold of about 0.025, and the 95% interval spans both negligible and clinically meaningful values. Therefore I do not accept it yet; I keep H37 unresolved and request independent validation because it is the strongest feature_065 candidate and the only plausible outcome-specific follow-up. The rest of the feature_065 cross-outcome screen is not supportive of a broad predictor: H38, H39, H40, and H41 are small and interval-crossing; H42, H43, and H44 are small, opposite, or interval-crossing. Given the number of correlated outcome tests and inconsistent directions, I reject and close these as not clinically meaningful. The new outcome_015 diversity screens H45, H46, H47, and H50 are also small and interval-crossing, with some opposite signs, so they are rejected and closed. I also reassess H16: although feature_065 remained direction-consistent on outcome_012 in discovery and validation, both point estimates are below the approximate 10% threshold and validation interval crosses zero; the broader outcome screen does not support feature_065 as a broad clinically meaningful predictor. I therefore reject and close H16 rather than continue chasing it. No leakage or coding problem is apparent: unique ID and constant features were avoided, all cells met the minimum sample-size rule, categorical levels are treated as nominal labels, and all estimates are interpreted as already signed to hypothesis direction. These are dataset-specific associations only, not causal or generalizability claims.

No new validation supports acceptance of any claim as clinically meaningful in this dataset. For the due H4 deadline, feature_002=1 versus 0 on outcome_006 had direction -1, so positive signed estimates correspond to more negative raw scores, i.e. stronger dependency. Discovery R4 was signed +0.0209 with a wide interval crossing zero, while independent validation R13 reversed to -0.0123 and its conservative validation interval also crossed zero and spanned the approximate 10% scale for outcome_006. The split-level disagreement and lack of a conservative interval above the clinical threshold argue against a robust association; H4 is rejected and closed. For H37, feature_065=1 versus 0 on outcome_015 was the only feature_065 candidate remaining: discovery R27 was signed +0.0211 [0.0018, 0.0404], excluding zero but lying below the approximate 10% absolute threshold for outcome_015 and including negligible effects in its lower half. Validation R39 reversed to -0.00825 [-0.0365, 0.0200] under the conservative validation alpha, crossing zero and not supporting the hypothesized direction. Together with the failed outcome_012 validation and the null/opposite cross-outcome feature_065 screen, this closes feature_065 as a clinically meaningful predictor. For H5, feature_034=1 versus 0 on outcome_006 had direction +1. Discovery R5 was negative and interval-crossing, while validation R40 was positive with point estimate above the approximate 10% threshold for outcome_006 but with a conservative interval that still crosses zero. Because the two splits disagree in direction and the validation uncertainty is not sufficient to support a clear clinically meaningful difference, H5 remains a negative/inconsistent signal and is rejected and closed. At this point the scientifically meaningful supported findings are none: the data provide negative evidence for feature_065, feature_002, and feature_034 on the outcomes tested, as well as most prior binary and subgroup contrasts. The remaining unresolved uncertainty is mainly the still-untested registered screens on outcome_012 and outcome_015, plus untested outcomes. The most informative next analysis is to continue registered diversity screens and new broad screens on less-covered outcomes, accepting only estimates with intervals that clearly exceed the approximate 10% scale and show consistency. These remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

No assessments are due. The evidence so far provides negative or inconclusive support for the previously pursued predictors, especially feature_065, feature_002, feature_034, and related subgroup contrasts. The next useful scientific question is whether any balanced binary or common nominal-category marker is associated with a clinically meaningful CRISPR dependency-score difference on outcomes that have been under-covered. I therefore propose a focused balanced-marker panel across outcome_003 and outcome_005, which are low-noise with approximate 10% absolute thresholds near 0.025, and outcome_011, which is somewhat noisier but untested and has an approximate 10% threshold near 0.030. The markers are feature_027, feature_052, feature_021, feature_020, feature_011, plus two common categorical contrasts: feature_036 level_001 versus level_002 and feature_048 level_001 versus level_003. All comparisons use direction -1 so that a positive signed estimate corresponds to the exposed category having a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. Because predictor names and labels are opaque, anticipated_direction is 0 rather than +1 or -1; the hypotheses are simply that any of these measured markers may confer either stronger dependency, weaker dependency, no meaningful difference, or an outcome-specific pattern. Categorical levels are nominal and are not treated as ordered. If a comparison yields a point estimate and uncertainty clearly at or above the relevant approximate 10% threshold and the interval excludes zero, it may become a candidate for validation or acceptance, especially if directionally coherent across outcomes. If the panel is mostly null, interval-crossing, or inconsistent, it should be closed as not supporting a clinically meaningful predictor. These are dataset-specific associations only, not causal claims or claims of generalizability. I avoid repeating closed feature_065, feature_002, feature_034, feature_042, and feature_045 contrasts, and I avoid the unique identifier and constant predictors.

No assessments are due, so this analysis batch should target the highest-information unresolved claims that are still untested. The most coherent remaining discovery plan is to complete a balanced binary-marker screen on two low-noise outcomes, outcome_012 and outcome_003, and to clear the deferred outcome_015 screens H48 and H49. For each outcome I test feature_027, feature_052, feature_021, feature_020, and feature_011 because these markers have reasonably common exposure prevalence, adequate expected cells, and high power relative to the approximately 10% absolute dependency-score threshold: about 0.025 for outcome_012 and outcome_003. All use direction -1, so a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has the more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. I also run H48, outcome_015 feature_023=1 versus 0, and H49, outcome_015 feature_032=1 versus 0. These clear previously deferred outcome_015 binary screens after the feature_065 family was closed. H49 is less balanced and lower powered than the binary markers on outcome_012/003, so I will interpret an interval-crossing or near-threshold H49 result cautiously. I defer outcome_005, outcome_011, categorical contrasts, and the remaining outcome_012 binary screens because of the 12-test cap. I am not reopening closed feature_065, feature_002, feature_034, feature_045, or feature_042 contrasts. Acceptance will require uncertainty excluding zero and a signed effect near or above the approximate 10% threshold; borderline interval-crossing signals will remain unresolved or be rejected rather than chased. All claims are dataset-specific associations only, not causal or generalizable claims.

All newly delivered discovery estimates fail the acceptance bar for a clinically meaningful association. With direction -1, a positive signed estimate corresponds to stronger dependency in the exposed group, but none of the intervals excludes zero in the hypothesized direction, and none has a signed point estimate clearly at or above the approximate 10% absolute scale. The closest case is H23: outcome_012 feature_020=1 versus 0 has signed estimate +0.0205 [-0.0007, 0.0418]. That point is only about 8.3% of the absolute mean for outcome_012, below the approximately 0.025 threshold, and its lower bound includes zero. Moreover, the same exposure on outcome_003 (H54) is essentially null and opposite-signed, so there is no cross-outcome coherence. Given that these 12 discovery tests used unadjusted 95% intervals and are not independent in outcome space, chasing H23 without a validation-quality signal would be vulnerable to multiplicity and split-level instability. H49 is also near the magnitude threshold in the opposite signed direction, but it is highly imbalanced (110 exposed, 1890 comparator), interval-crossing, and lower powered, so it does not support a scientifically meaningful difference. The remaining results for feature_027, feature_052, feature_021, feature_011, feature_023, and the rest of the screen are small, interval-crossing, or directionally inconsistent. No leakage, coding, or eligibility problem is apparent: all cells met the minimum sample-size requirement, nominal categorical levels were not treated as ordered, and unique/constant predictors were avoided. No independent validation is requested because none of these candidates reaches the evidence strength appropriate for validation; validation is better reserved for a comparison with an interval excluding zero and a point estimate at or beyond the clinical scale, preferably with some coherence.

The response deadline for H16 is now resolved by the delivered validation evidence. H16 tested feature_065=1 versus 0 on outcome_012 with direction -1, so a positive signed estimate corresponds to the exposed group having the more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. The discovery estimate was +0.0169 with a 95% interval of [-0.0027, 0.0365], and the independent validation estimate was +0.0194 with a conservative validation interval of [-0.0094, 0.0482]. Both intervals cross zero, and neither provides a statistically credible signal under the validation-level uncertainty. The magnitudes are also below the approximate clinically meaningful absolute scale for outcome_012: using the absolute mean as the scale, a 10% difference is around 0.025, while the signed points are about 0.017 and 0.019. The lower bounds include effects near zero and the upper bounds are driven by wide uncertainty rather than a robust large shift. Combined with the earlier feature_065 screen across other outcomes and the failed feature_065 validation on outcome_015, this closes H16 and the feature_065 predictor family as not supporting a clinically meaningful association in this dataset.

The accepted-claim set remains empty. The evidence so far is negative or inconclusive for all tested predictors, including feature_065, feature_002, feature_034, feature_045, feature_042, and the recent outcome_012/outcome_003 binary marker screens. The main remaining uncertainty is not a borderline validated signal, but rather whether any marker has an outcome-specific effect on less-covered outcomes such as outcome_005 and outcome_011. The next most informative analysis is therefore to complete the balanced binary-marker panel on these outcomes: feature_027, feature_052, feature_021, feature_020, and feature_011. The five outcome_005 claims H58-H62 are already registered, and H63-H64 already cover feature_027 and feature_021 on outcome_011. I registered the remaining outcome_011 markers feature_052, feature_020, and feature_011 so that the next analysis can run a coherent 10-test outcome_005/outcome_011 panel. Other active untested claims, especially outcome_012 binary contrasts H27-H30 and categorical contrasts H33-H36, should be deferred unless a strong signal appears. Future acceptance should still require an interval that excludes zero in the hypothesized direction and a signed estimate at or above the approximate 10% absolute outcome scale, with extra caution for noisy outcomes: roughly 0.025 for outcome_005 and 0.030 for outcome_011. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal effects or generalizable claims.

No assessments are due. The strongest current priority is the already registered 10-test balanced binary-marker panel on outcome_005 and outcome_011: feature_027, feature_052, feature_021, feature_020, and feature_011. That panel should be executed first because it uses reasonably common exposures, avoids low-prevalence instability, and targets two outcomes with approximate clinically meaningful absolute scales near 0.025 for outcome_005 and 0.030 for outcome_011. To make the next batch more informative and diverse within the 12-test capacity, I registered two high-power categorical contrasts using feature_054, level_002 versus level_001. feature_054 has favorable nominal-cell sizes, with top level_001 occurring 1422 times and level_002 occurring 578 times, so both comparison cells should meet the minimum cell requirement and provide power near the clinical threshold. The previously tested outcome_012 feature_054 contrast was small and interval-crossing, but it does not establish that feature_054 lacks association on outcome_005 or outcome_011. These are hypothesis-generating outcome-specific comparisons only. Direction is set to -1 so that a positive signed estimate means level_002 has the more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. Because predictor names and labels are opaque, anticipated_direction is 0: the data may show stronger dependency, weaker dependency, no clinically meaningful difference, or an outcome-specific pattern. Acceptance should require a signed point estimate at or above the relevant approximate 10% absolute threshold and an interval excluding zero, preferably with some coherence or validation. If both feature_054 contrasts are null, opposite-signed, or near-threshold with intervals crossing zero, I would close feature_054 after considering the prior outcome_012 result. If one of the active binary markers or feature_054 produces a clean clinically meaningful signal, the next step should be cross-outcome checking and, if needed, validation. If the panel is null overall, future exploration should shift toward less-covered outcomes or common categorical predictors such as feature_019, feature_036, feature_048, feature_055, and feature_009, but only using contrasts likely to have adequate cells. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

No assessments are due, so the analysis stage should request the 12 highest-information untested active comparisons. I selected the complete balanced binary-marker panel for outcome_005 and outcome_011: feature_027, feature_052, feature_021, feature_020, and feature_011, plus the two high-cell-size nominal categorical feature_054 contrasts, level_002 versus level_001. These targets are scientifically useful because outcome_005 and outcome_011 have not yet been screened with the same broadly available marker set, and these markers avoid rare exposures that produced unstable or low-powered comparisons elsewhere. Each comparison uses direction -1, so the signed returned estimate is oriented so that a positive value means the exposed group or nominal level has the more negative CRISPR dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. I do not assume a direction for any opaque predictor: anticipated direction is uncertain. Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and require at least 20 observations per cell; these exposures have favorable prevalence, although outcome_011 is noisier and thus should require an effect near or above its approximate 10% absolute scale, around 0.030. For outcome_005, the approximate 10% absolute scale is around 0.025. If the results are small, interval-crossing, opposite-signed, or only near threshold, I will reject or close the relevant marker family rather than request validation. If a marker shows a clear clinically meaningful association with an interval excluding zero and some cross-outcome coherence, the next stage should pursue targeted follow-up or validation.

All twelve comparisons use direction -1, so a positive signed estimate would mean the exposed group/level has the more negative CRISPR dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. Most results are clinically negligible and interval-crossing. For outcome_005, the approximate 10% absolute-mean scale is about 0.025; for outcome_011 it is about 0.030. H58-H59, H61-H63, H65-H66, and H68-H69 have small point estimates with intervals crossing zero, so I reject and close those comparisons. H60 (outcome_005 feature_021) has a signed estimate of -0.0201 with an interval entirely below zero, indicating an opposite-direction raw association, but the magnitude is only about 8% of the outcome_005 absolute mean and below the clinical threshold; the registered direction is not supported and this specific reversal is not worth pursuing. H67 (outcome_011 feature_011) has a signed estimate of -0.0330 with an interval excluding zero, also opposite to the registered direction, but its magnitude is about 11% of the outcome_011 absolute mean, making it the only new comparison with a clinically relevant point estimate and nominal exclusion of zero. However, its lower bound is very close to zero, it emerged from a 12-test screen, and it contradicts the original direction, so I reject the original directional claim but keep it active pending independent validation. Validation will indicate whether this apparently meaningful opposite association is robust enough to justify a refined reversed claim. No coding or eligibility problems are apparent: all cells met minimum size, nominal categories were treated as labels, and unique/constant predictors were avoided. All interpretations remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

The delivered validation results support negative conclusions for all three response-deadline/new-validation claims. For H37, outcome_015 feature_065=1 versus 0 with direction -1, the discovery result was +0.0211 with an interval just above zero, but it is below the approximate 10% absolute-mean scale for outcome_015 (about 0.025) and the independent validation estimate was -0.0083 with a conservative interval crossing zero and opposite in direction. This does not support the hypothesized clinically meaningful association, so H37 remains rejected and is closed. For H5, outcome_006 feature_034=1 versus 0 with direction +1, discovery was negative and interval-crossing; validation was positive around +0.030, but the conservative validation interval still crossed zero.
